sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $23.7 billion to $51.8 billion [F1][F10][F168].
The path was cyclical rather than steady: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then jumped 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][F6][F7][D161][D200][D238].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion and has grown only 4.9% in FY2025, leaving the three-year CAGR at -5.3% [F8][F10][D274][D342][D844].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth, while non-U.S. added 2.0pp [D382][D384][D400][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but grew only 0.1%, contributing 0.1pp, while natural gas grew 37.4% and added 4.4pp [D551][D552][D553][D585][D586].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 against revenue growth of 4.9%, and EPS fell 18.7% as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [F20][D343][D342][D344][D356].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025, faster than the 4.9% revenue growth [D352][D342].
Net margin of 15.4% in FY2025 sits below the 17.9% window median and far below the 30.6% FY2022 high, though above the -19.8% FY2020 low [F30][D831][D830][D829].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, with D&A at 19.5% of revenue and cost of revenue at 37.9% [D351][D330][D326].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025 mainly on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
The effective tax rate of 36.9% in FY2025 exceeded the 32.4% of FY2024, and net margin sat 15.4% against a 36.9% tax rate [D332][D298][F30].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 1.52x of FY2022 [F59][F20][D333][D226].
The FY2025 decrease from $20.1 billion in FY2024 came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 and was 23.1% in FY2022, against a 12.2% window median [D185][D223][D834].
Capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 1.35x D&A, while stock-based compensation was 1.7% of operating cash flow in FY2025 [D222][D228][D334].
Net cash of $7.1 billion was 12.1% of revenue in FY2025, in the 100th percentile of six energy peers against a -7.7% median [D337][D338][D850][D851].
In FY2025 cash went to $12.6 billion of capital spending, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the 30% framework [P31][D339][F59].
Return on average equity of 12.4% in FY2025 was in the 33rd percentile of six peers against a 14.9% median [D341][D852][D853].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10][R1].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix a recast year with a never-recast year rest on two presentations, so the trend should be read with that caveat [R1].
Revenue declined 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion [F8][D274][R2].
The decline was primarily due to lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P47].
A single price-driven down year in a cyclical upstream portfolio is a normal swing rather than a structural break [R2].
Whether net margin holds above the 15.4% of FY2025 or falls toward the 17.9% median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D831].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the $19.8 billion of FY2025 or drops toward the $20.0 billion of FY2023, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F59][F57].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the 12.1% of FY2025, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D338].
